problem_text:
A logistics manager needs to distribute a total shipment volume across 11 regional distribution centers to maximize overall delivery efficiency.  
The performance metrics and capacity limits for each center are as follows:  
* Center A: efficiency score 0.036, resource usage 0.286, capacity range [0.081, 0.453]  
* Center B: efficiency score 0.098, resource usage 0.162, capacity range [0.027, 0.362]  
* Center C: efficiency score 0.102, resource usage 0.237, capacity range [0.006, 0.644]  
* Center D: efficiency score 0.130, resource usage 0.219, capacity range [0.071, 0.734]  
* Center E: efficiency score 0.076, resource usage 0.058, capacity range [0.058, 0.437]  
* Center F: efficiency score 0.154, resource usage 0.047, capacity range [0.008, 0.605]  
* Center G: efficiency score 0.153, resource usage 0.237, capacity range [0.046, 0.326]  
* Center H: efficiency score 0.041, resource usage 0.088, capacity range [0.036, 0.818]  
* Center I: efficiency score 0.147, resource usage 0.267, capacity range [0.050, 0.447]  
* Center J: efficiency score 0.146, resource usage 0.234, capacity range [0.057, 0.583]  
* Center K: efficiency score 0.049, resource usage 0.019, capacity range [0.037, 0.530]  

Each center must be allocated a fraction of the total shipment volume within its specified capacity range, and the sum of all allocation fractions must equal one.  
To ensure rapid response capability, the manager requires that the high-priority centers, represented by the set L = {F, J}, together handle at least 0.248 of the total volume.  
Additionally, the total resource usage of the distribution network must not exceed 0.170, and the overall efficiency score must be at least 0.091.  
Determine the optimal shipment allocation fractions that maximize the total efficiency score while satisfying all constraints.
